Thank you Salivan.

This is why I am looking in to origins and targets as being part of the missing 'piece'. Zone 1 would be the origin of the move down, and even more significant if it also was the target for longs (originating at zone 2).

The market moves depending on order flow. We focus mainly on engulfs of important FL's in to a PAZ for an indication of where price is preparing to go next. The engulf is only valid if its target hasn't been hit, and IF says "every engulf has a specific target".

Lets assume a bearish engulf happens:

If there is a bearish engulf on a HTF chart, there will be an associated target (the origin of the last move up?). Until that target is hit we would be taking a big risk taking any long position...even if we found a bullish engulf into a different PAZ in a lower time frame.Until the HTF engulf hits its intended target, the prevailing momentum of the market won't change. We wouldn't feel safe getting in to a trade if we were in the middle of a PAZ in the HTF...IF also tells us to trade only the edges of these zones.

Just because there is an engulf on a LTF at an extreme edge of a flag doesn't mean we are at an extreme area on the higher time frame. We might still be stuck in the middle of a PAZ. Maybe the missing piece is knowing when the HTF and LTF engulfs and final orders/liquidity line up with each other...? Wouldn't we anticipate the largest volume of orders be located in these target areas?

Maybe that is why Salivan and IF and other experienced traders on RTM always say "look left, and look left again". Maybe we have to first track all of the engulfs and their targets before knowing if the trade we are about to take is being executed in a low risk/high return area. Not sure, but its worth thinking about

Quick disclaimer: I honestly have no idea if this is correct....Just my recent thoughts.

What caught my attention yesterday when I was explaining my analogy of the tornado, is the new high that engulfs the origin of the move down (at the very top of my drawing). The new high that forms EG "B" also makes all the PA part of FL Box "X" and it makes FL "Z" a FTR/FL. Salivan mentioned trades occurring at FL's which were at the extreme edges of a different FL....maybe that is what he's talking about? In this example, the trade occurs at the last area of liquidity at the edge of FL Box "X".

The last of the OF would occur at the FTR/FL that forms after the engulf of the decision to fakeout. I marked that area on the drawing too.

We could easily take a long position at that light blue flag once price made a deep RT because of the following reasons:

1. This is a FTR that formed after the engulf of the decision to fakeout.

2. FL "C" is formed when price returns to FL "Z" on its FTB. This eliminates the OF in the dark blue rectangle that represents the Fl of FL Box "X". We don't have to worry about price faking out to the extreme of FL Z because there are no orders left. It would be pointless for IT's to push price down there.

4. The fakeout already took all the orders in FL "C". The tornado touched down Pushing price back down in to the low of the fakeout is pointless...no more orders left.

5. Engulf B (top of the drawing) tells us price is looking to move up over the long term.

6. FL Box "X" is located at a flip zone. FL Box "X" is holding price up. The low of FL Box "X" didn't engulf anything important to the left (we can't see that from this drawing but I am assuming this is the case for the purposes of this example).

I am ready to take a stab at a live trade this upcoming week. The pair I am focused on is EUR-AUD. I will post some charts to explain why I think a good opportunity exists to short this pair.

** I modeled this trade exactly off my conceptual drawing on Post # 813.

First, a basic HTF chart to show major levels I will be focusing on.

4-Hour Chart with entry order shown:

I am not 100% confident in the entry order's placement, because while price has returned to the origin of the engulf, it hasn't reached the MPL of the FL yet, and there are a couple of nice supply levels still untouched. The stop placement is a bit high for my R:R.

It is possible that price has already faked out and in the process of finishing a QM before dropping. If price were to drop near the level it is currently at, it would be needlessly leaving behind lots of sell orders....

I will zoom in and see if I can refine the entry.

Here is a 30-Min chart showing my refined entry. On the next chart I will zoom in to the red rectangle (origin of the engulf) to show why I lowered my stop and refined my entry.

The chart below is also a 30-min chart, but it focuses on the details of the decision to engulf (red rectangle). Since the origin of the engulf is a large Flag on a daily time frame, there are a few choices to look for price to turn once the chart is zoomed in. As I looked closer, I saw that a majority of the orders had already been consumed in the flag. I set my entry at a level equal to the last supply zone, also in an area where price has a lot of history bouncing/faking out. The stop loss was lowered to the top of the last remaining set of orders. Stop loss 25 pips, limit approximately 720 pips (1:28 RR).

Might be a bit ambitious, but it's a demo so I'm going to set the order and see what happens.

Lastly, the reason for my target being where it is:

A bullish QM level at the origin of a move up.

OK, one last chart....

I wanted to mark the detail of the possible diamond formation - I suspect there will be lots of sellers when the market open tomorrow since price is entering (what looks to be) a strong supply zone. I drew two colored lines on the chart below:

Neon Green & Purple

Neon Green Dotted line = Retail traders (supply and demand traders mostly) entry short Neon Green Solid line = Retail traders stop loss

Purple Dotted line = Retail traders entry (breakout traders getting long on the break of "swing high". Purple Solid line = estimated location for the breakout trader's stops

By pushing price above the HH portion of the QM, IT's will be triggering massive amounts of orders to give them liquidity for the move down. (of course that is only true if I am correct about price getting ready to drop)...which I could be totally wrong about
